rationale: The Old English place-name element *Baroc-scír* (Berkshire) is traditionally derived from a reference to a notable oak tree (or oak forest) used as a landmark or meeting point, referring to the living tree rather than its timber. The tree sense (oak.n.02) fits a toponym anchored to a specific oak as a geographic feature, whereas the wood/material sense (oak.n.01) would be incidental to place-name formation.
